evidence.description: The init method launches a Task to retrieve credentials, which completes asynchronously after the object is already initialized and potentially accessible.

candidates.explanation: The initializer performs an asynchronous operation (retrieveStoredCredentials) inside a Task block. This creates a race condition where the object's properties might be accessed by other parts of the application before the initialization task completes, leading to inconsistent initial states.
candidates.title: Asynchronous Side Effect in Initializer

evidence.description: The userProfile didSet observer uses Task { @MainActor in ... } to post a notification.

candidates.explanation: The `userProfile` property uses a `didSet` observer that spawns a new `Task` to post a notification on the `@MainActor`. This pattern can lead to out-of-order notifications if multiple updates occur in rapid succession, as there is no guarantee of execution order for independent Tasks.
candidates.title: Unordered Notifications in didSet

evidence.description: setupTokensWithCredentials launches a Task to call dispatchAuthStateChange instead of awaiting it.

candidates.explanation: The `setupTokensWithCredentials` method spawns a new `Task` to dispatch state changes. This is an anti-pattern in an actor where the caller might expect the state change to be part of the current execution flow; instead, it creates a detached execution that may complete after subsequent operations have already started.
candidates.title: Detached Task for State Dispatch

evidence.description: The method checks if auth0Provider is an instance of NativeToWebSSOAuth0Provider to call getSSOCredentials().

candidates.explanation: The `retrieveSSOCredentials` method uses a conditional downcast to a specific concrete type (`NativeToWebSSOAuth0Provider`) to access functionality. This violates the Dependency Inversion Principle and makes the service tightly coupled to a specific implementation of the `Auth0ProviderProtocol`.
candidates.title: Tight Coupling via Downcasting
